newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania says press curbs do not breach rights.
newsitem.headline: Albania says press curbs do not breach rights.

text.p: The Albanian government defended emergency measures curbing press freedoms on Tuesday and said the restrictions did not breach international conventions.
Parliament voted on Sunday to introduce a state of emergency and ordered domestic media to submit to official control in the Balkan nation, where armed unrest has swept towns in the south.
The 140-seat legislature is dominated by President Sali Berisha's embattled Democratic Party.

"The press and information department (of the Foreign Ministry) confirms that the establishment of a state of emergency concerning freedom of information is totally based on the law and at the same time on international treaties of which Albania is part," a ministry statement said.
A justice ministry spokesman, Agim Neza, said the curbs did not apply to foreign news organisations. "You are free to report," Neza told Reuters.
He noted that the statement advised journalists not to travel to towns in the south where the government could not guarantee their safety.
Western governments and international watchdog groups have criticised the state of emergency measures for the media as censorship and called on the government to lift them.
The Foreign Ministry statement said the emergency ruling was in accordance with European and United Nations civil rights conventions.

"The press and information department...is sure that foreign journalists and correspondents will respect standards of information and it guarantees them its full readiness to help them," the statement said.

It said it was inadvisable for foreign journalists to travel to parts of the south, where government forces are struggling to wrest control from armed rioters protesting at the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes.
"According to the Interior Ministry, the situation in some towns in the south is still not under the control of state institutions.
"Thus the Interior Ministry has advised foreign citizens that it does not offer guarantees for them in the above mentioned zone," it said.
State television had been instructed to make its facilities available to foreign camera crews following an interruption to broadcasting from the lone foreign satellite feed in Tirana.
The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) said on Monday that Albanian authorities had suspended its licence to transmit film by satellite from Albania.
The ministry statement said it regretted incidents of inaccurate reporting by the media.
